# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

Extracting a chunk here is the cleanest way to shave ~10+ CC from action.

Extraction plan (TDD-safe — behavior-preserving split):
- `postCompletionPrComment(scm, pr, ticketKey, fixSummary, fixSummaryWithWarnings, repliesPosted, nonBlockingGateWarningBlock, codeChangesCommitted)` → returns prCommentPosted. Contains hasMeaningfulSummary + the 3-way branch (≈4 branches + try/catch).

That's big (~180 lines, many branches) — extracting it wholesale removes a LOT of CC from action (maybe too much at once, but it's mechanical, pure-ish orchestration with the same mocks available).

But careful: these helpers use module-level functions (postPRComment, headMovedSinceLastReview, prHasApproved, removeConfiguredLabels, postJiraComment, buildCompletionLiveState, postLapMarker, readReworkBaseHead, LABELS, github_remove_label...). All same-module — fine.

However — CRAP counts per function; a new big helper will have its own CRAP — it must stay ≤ 8 or be small enough. The tail block has many branches: ~15+ decisions → CC maybe 20+ → CRAP over threshold → NEW over-threshold failure! Must split into 2-3 moderate helpers, each ≤ 8 CRAP... at 75% coverage CC 14 gives CRAP ~17 — too high. CC 10 at 75% → 11.6 — still over 8! Hmm — new functions must have CRAP ≤ 8. At cov ~75%, CC must be ≤ ~6?? CC 6: 36·0.0156+6=6.56 ✓. CC 7: 49·0.0156+7=7.76 ✓. CC 8: 64·0.0156+8=9.0 ✗. So new helpers need CC ≤ 7 (at 75% cov) unless coverage is higher. With 90% cov: (0.1)³=0.001 → CC 20 → 0.4+20 = 20.4... wait no: CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC. cov 0.9 → (1−cov)³ = 0.001. CC 20 → 400·0.001+20 = 20.4. Hmm CRAP is dominated by CC at high coverage. So even at 90% cov, CC must be ~≤8 for CRAP ≤ 8.3. At 95%: CC 10 → 100·0.000125+10 = 10.01. So basically new functions need CC ≤ 8 (or ≤ 9-10 at near-100% coverage).

So: extract SEVERAL small helpers (CC ≤ 7 each). From the tail:
1. `postCompletionPrComment(...)` — CC ~5 ✓

So the fixes needed:

2. **`loadPushReworkChangesForAction`** (test helper): 21 → 23, must get back to ≤ 21. It's the test loader I extended with mocks. Reduce by 2 CC — e.g., extract a small helper from its body (or simplify a conditional chain).

TDD approach:
- For `action`: the "reproducing test" is the ratchet itself (CI-failing measurement). Behavior-preserving extraction; suites must stay green. I'll extract:
 a. `postCompletionPrComment(...)` — Block A (PR comment decision).
 b. `finalizeTicketState(tracker, ticketKey, statuses, actualParams, customParams)` — Blocks B+D+E (status move, assign-back, WIP label, SM labels).

 e. `stampCompletionLapMarker(scm, pr, ticketKey, lapGate, lapResolutions)` — Block J.

Ground truth — exactly **2 regressions**:

1. `js/pushReworkChanges.js::action`: 263.3 → 288.5
2. `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js::loadPushReworkChangesForAction`: 21 → 23

Everything else improved or is new-below-threshold (0 new over threshold).

So the fixes needed:
1. **`action`**: extract tail blocks to bring CRAP ≤ 263.3 (CC ≤ ~102 at 75.3% cov; each −1 CC ≈ −3 CRAP; need −25 CRAP ≈ −8 CC).
2. **`loadPushReworkChangesForAction`** (test helper): 21 → 23, must get back to ≤ 21. It's the test loader I extended with mocks. Reduce by 2 CC — e.g., extract a small helper from its body (or simplify a conditional chain).

TDD approach:
- For `action`: the "reproducing test" is the ratchet itself (CI-failing measurement). Behavior-preserving extraction; suites must stay green. I'll extract:
 a. `postCompletionPrComment(...)` — Block A (PR comment decision).
 b. `finalizeTicketState(tracker, ticketKey, statuses, actualParams, customParams)` — Blocks B+D+E (status move, assign-back, WIP label, SM labels).
 c. `reviewLatchDecisions(...)` split into: `stickyApprovalNotice(scm, pr, stickyApproved)`, `noopRearmOrThreadNote(scm, tracker, pr, ticketKey, stickyApproved, freshReviewWanted, resolvedCount)`, `clearAiReviewedLatch(scm, pr, freshReviewWanted)` (Block G).
 d. `runAutoStartReview(autoStart, scm, config, ticketKey, params, actualParams, customParams, freshReviewWanted, stickyApproved)` — Block H incl. triggerSmIfIdle.
 e. `stampCompletionLapMarker(scm, pr, ticketKey, lapGate, lapResolutions)` — Block J.
 f. `postCompletionTokenUsage(params)` — Block K (try/catch around tokenUsageComment).

 Removing from action: Block A (≈5 decisions), B+D+E (≈5), F/G (≈12: sticky if+tc, noop if(4cond)+2tc, resolved-log if(4cond), fresh if(4cond)+tc), H (≈8), I (1), K (1) ≈ 32 decisions → CC 109 → ~77. CRAP ≈ 77²·0.0156+77 = 169. 

 But new helpers must each be ≤ CRAP 8:
 - postCompletionPrComment: CC ~6 (if, if, tc, elseif(2cond), else) → CRAP at ~85% cov ≈ 36·(0.15³≈0.0034)+6 ≈ 6.1 ✓
 - finalizeTicketState: CC ~6 → ✓ (coverage from existing action tests)
 - stickyApprovalNotice: CC ~3 ✓
 - noopRearmOrThreadNote: CC ~7 (if 4-cond + 2 tc + if 4-cond) → 49·0.0034+7 ≈ 7.2 ✓
 - clearAiReviewedLatch: CC ~4 ✓
 - runAutoStartReview: split into skipReason + trigger: wrapper CC ~6, skipReason CC ~5, triggerReviewStart CC ~2 ✓
 - stampCompletionLapMarker: CC ~3 ✓
 - postCompletionTokenUsage: CC ~2 ✓

2. For `loadPushReworkChangesForAction`: read it, find 2+ decisions to extract (e.g., a `resolveMocks(mocks)` or simplify an options branch). Let me read it.

Also note: CI measures with the exact same values (75.3% cov on action) — my replica's coverage matched CI's precisely (988KB cov file; CI report shows identical CC/cov/CRAP). Good.

Then re-run: local ratchet must show these two fixed. My local replica had broken baseline matching — fix that: the issue might be the recursive `agents` symlink producing weird path keys in the coverage json OR crap4js mismatch. But interesting: my replica's FUNCTION measurements were fine (they appear in the report); only the baseline DIFF failed ("526 removed"). Since CI's diff works with the same inputs, the difference must be my environment. Hypothesis: the released baseline's keys are `js/...::fn` while my run's current-set keys became `/tmp/inst2/js/...::fn` or `agents/js/...`. CI's keys would be `$RUNER_TEMP/inst`-rooted too... but CI works. One difference: my symlink /tmp/inst2/agents → /tmp/inst2 created a real recursive walk. In CI, same symlink — hmm.

Actually wait: maybe the mismatch is coverage-json keys. My cov json keys: probably `/tmp/inst2/js/...`. crap4js probably resolves them relative to the report dir. If it doesn't, mismatch → all removed. In CI, RUNER_TEMP=/home/runer/work/_temp — also absolute. So CI would mismatch too... unless crap4js strips the common prefix. CI works, I don't — maybe because my tree has the extra `agents/` recursion making the common-prefix computation fail or producing duplicate function entries that collide.

Found the bug in my replica: the `agents` symlink created a recursive directory walk — `crap4js .` walked into `agents/` (the self-symlink) generating `agents/agents/agents/...` entries and blowing up the report. In CI the same symlink exists (`ln -sfn "$RUNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNER_TEMP/inst/agents"`)... hmm, CI does the same! But CI's crap4js run — how does it avoid the recursion? Maybe crap4js doesn't follow symlinks, and in CI it works; here the `agents/` entries in my report suggest it DID follow. Wait — the report shows `agents/agents/agents/...` — recursion happened. But CI would hit the same...

Unless in CI the symlink target layout differs. Actually maybe the issue: `ln -sfn /tmp/inst2 /tmp/inst2/agents` — if /tmp/inst2/agents ALREADY EXISTED as a directory (from nyc instrument or rsync), ln -sfn creates the symlink INSIDE it (agents/agents). Then the walk recursion is real and CI would fail too... but CI's crap run DID produce a real verdict (it failed with regressions, meaning it matched the baseline).

Hmm, wait — actually in CI the symlink is created right after `nyc instrument`, BEFORE rsync. Same as mine. Then `crap4js .` — if crap4js skips symlinked dirs, no recursion. My report HAS agents/ entries — so either crap4js followed it, or... rsync copied something? No.

Key difference: my /tmp/inst2/agents symlink points to /tmp/inst2 itself — infinite loop. crap4js apparently followed it (with some depth limit). The report is polluted but the KEY question is whether the function rows for real files are present and matched the baseline. "526 removed, 0 new" says no matches happened. Why?

Look at report rows: `cov_1rgb4158n2 .dmtools/config.js` — the METHOD names are Istanbul coverage helper names (`cov_...`)! The report is reading INSTRUMENTED files?? No wait — `crap4js .` runs on the tree at /tmp/inst2 which IS instrumented (nyc instrument rewrote all .js with coverage counters!). In CI, crap4js also runs on the instrumented tree — that's how it correlates coverage. The `cov_1rgb...` method at the top is from `.dmtools/config.js` — an instrumented file where function names got mangled?

Hmm, but in my earlier (previous session) replica, the report had clean names like `action js/pushReworkChanges.js 109 ...`. What changed? In the previous session, I ran the same steps... and got a working ratchet with named functions.

Difference: previous session I compared against a baseline built from the merge-base (`crap-baseline.json` written by --write-baseline locally) — the comparison "worked" because both sides came from the same tool/invocation. Now the RELEASED baseline has keys `js/agentDocGenerator.js::add` — format `file::function`. The report rows are `function file cc cov crap`. crap4js --baseline must map them. If mapping worked, we'd see matches. "526 removed" = no matches at all.

So how does CI pass/fail correctly? Maybe CI's baseline comparison uses file paths from the COVERAGE json (relative to cwd) and matches `file::name`. My coverage-final.json keys — let me check: they might be `/tmp/inst2/js/...` absolute, so `js/...` relative mismatch → no match → all removed → vacuous pass. CI would have the same issue though... unless in CI, `$RUNER_TEMP/inst` paths make nyc emit relative keys.

Actually the important realization: I can't fully explain CI's behavior from here, but I CAN check what the ACTUAL CI run measured — the job log! The CI failure details link: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39039468518/job/117415966290.    - `runAutoStartReview` + `autoStartReviewSkipReason` + `triggerAutoStartReview` + `ticketOf` — the opt-in pr_review auto-start with its three skip reasons, failure degradation and SM idle-wake.

The rework pass is complete.

## Summary

**Root cause found via CI ground truth**: the `crap` ratchet compares against a **rolling release baseline** (`crap-baseline` @ main@92e678ba), not the merge-base — after the main-side merges ratcheted the baseline down, my previous pass's "green" local run (against a stale baseline) missed that `action` (288.5) exceeded the 263.3 baseline. I pulled the exact CI verdict from the failed job log: **2 regressions** — `pushReworkChanges.action` 263.3→288.5 and test helper `loadPushReworkChangesForAction` 21→23.

**Fixes (TDD: CI ratchet was the failing test, reproduced locally with pinned crap4js + nyc + the released baseline)**:
- Extracted `action`'s ~200-line completion tail into 15 small exported helpers (`postCompletionPrComment`, `finalizeTicketState`, `noopLapDecisions`, `runAutoStartReview`, `stampCompletionLapMarker`, …) — behavior-preserving, pinned by a new 12-test suite.
- Added `opt()` accessor in the test loader (−6 decisions).
- Cliff-edge hardening: split `wipLabelOf` so `finalizeTicketState` sits at CC 6, not the CC-8 coverage cliff.

**Verified against the released baseline**: action 288.5→**53.2** (baseline 263.3), loader 23→**17** (baseline 21); all 16 new functions at CC ≤ 7 with verified coverage entries; full suite **3465/3465**; target suite **107/107**. Open discussion entries are all no-id system records → `review_replies.json` is `{"replies": []}`.
